title: The Keeper of the Last Wet Well
openingText: He meets you at the wellhead rather than the gate. The gate is a formality, the well is the town. Two of his people keep crossbows level at the horizon behind him, watching the heat instead of you. 'Everyone who walks in here wants the same thing and pretends otherwise. So: you want water. I want the road open and my people breathing. Tell me what you're carrying that's worth a drink.'
openingTextLate: Sahl meets you at the wellhead with twice the guard and half the patience. The horizon his people watch has begun watching back. 'The well still holds,' he says. 'That sentence is doing more work every season. Say what you want.'
dialogueWalkawayLate: We're done. The road out is the one you came in on, and it is worse than it was. Walk it before noon anyway.
dialogueWalkaway: We're done. The road out is the one you came in on. Walk it before noon.
dialogueAccept: Done. Draw what you're owed, and don't come back thirsty and empty-handed.
confidence: The cistern is lower than the ledger says. Sahl is rationing the garrison and calling it discipline.

clauses.text: Standing draw from the garrison cistern: 25 supplies of water and salt-pork out of the Well-Captain's own stores.
The garrison honors its standing bounty on dust-raiders: 45 gold, and the roadbound remember who collected it.
Every drop drawn here is accounted for. The ledger says the guild owes 35 gold against it.
The next caravan out is provisioned at the guild's expense: 15 supplies, pledged from your own stores.
Their dispositions: where every picket and camp on this ground stands
Safe conduct under their banner: no patrol will trouble you
Provisions from your stores for their line
Your party stands a watch on their line
